questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
- English speaking country
- Cultural connection 
- Very good university
- International environment

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was a little difficult at first, but once I got in the loop everything worked out fine

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received contact information for all the people responsible for student wellfare, but I never need assistance so I didn't really look for it either.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very difficult and very expensive, however what I found ended up being cheaper/same price as the student housing. I am very happy I stayed in private accommodation as it forced me to meet people in different ways than I would have done if I had stayed in University accommodation. I recommend subscribing to as many Facebook housing groups as possible, as that is how I found my accommodation.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Edinburgh isn't a very big city and living off campus gives you the opportunity to discover all that is outside city center, which I can't recommend enough. I wouldn't stray too far away, but public transport is very well functioning so even if that happens to become the case, it isn't too much of a problem.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I received an email about a drop in for student registration and went to get registered during the time slot I had been notified about.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I am not sure, as I didn't really need help I didn't look for it either.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was very successful, and I was even able to change to a course I preferred after the exchange had started as I found out one of the other ones that I had gotten wasn't really for me.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is fun to try different subjects and explore other areas of academia than what you usually do, I recommend trying across-subject courses such as Astrobiology, which I found very giving. I also throughly enjoyed the high academic level of teaching in the more advanced courses I took, but whether you want to take a hard course or keep it easy to have some more free time of course depends on what your goals are with the exchange.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic level of the courses I took I found very high compared to the ones at my home University, however I was taking a more advanced course than what I have been able to do at home so that explains it.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: University of Edinburgh focused more on actually learning the material rather than learning for the exam, an aspect of UCPH which I haven't really enjoyed so I was very happy to try something else.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Astrobiology
Meteorology: Atmosphere and Environment
RNP: Relativity, Particle and Nuclear Physics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Astrobiology is definitely a recommendation, as it is a very broad course that really connects a lot of different subjects and gives you a lot of knowledge you wouldn't have been able to gather otherwise.
RNP is also very giving if you are interested in particle and nuclear physics, but it is a hard course that expects a lot of background knowledge in Physics and many hours of work to understand the material throughly.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Many of the private housing listings are only for the rent, all bills are added on top afterwards and they can get as high as 100£ per month in the winter months when heating is turned on.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries were a lot less expensive than expected!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a club/society for everything, from fashion to netball to mountaineering to contemporary art.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really recommend going ceilidh dancing, either with the society or on your own. It is a very cultural experience and so much fun wether you're a dancer or not.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Going on a highland trip to explore Scotland is a must, other than that wandering around the city is magical on its own and you can really spend a lot of time exploring all of Edinburghs little streets and corners.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy, it isn't very different from the one at home.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to people! It seems very scary at first, but once you start you'll realise you can make friends even while standing in line at the grocery store.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None really

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The kilts and back pipes! Scottish people are proud to be scottish, and it is so much fun to get to experience that.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Pack a raincoat, if you think it rains in Copenhagen you're in for a big surprise. In Edinburgh it can somehow rain from all directions at the same time, so an umbrella won't save you.
Get to know some locals! Edinburgh is a very international environment and the University is full of people from all around the world, so it is a lot of fun to get to know people who actually come from the city rather than sticking to being friends with all the other exchange students.
Take the difficult course! It has given me so much clarity about my upcoming bachelors project and even though it did take away from my free time, I am so happy I did it. The exchange isn't only about making friends around the world - don't underestimate the power of academic contacts at a university that ranks as good as University of Edinburgh does.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: King's Building is a little far out from city center, about a 45 minute walk from the main campus: so make sure not to take courses that are one right after the other but located in two different places.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Finding people I genuinely connected with, both in friendships and academic relations

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: In the beginning it was finding people I felt I could connect with, as many of the other exchange students from UCPH were in fields very that were very different from mine - but when I moved my focus outside of this small group, I was able to find people I now dare call friends for life, so everything fell right into place anyway.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
